title: Private Deployments - VPC & On-Prem Reference Architectures and Day-2 Ops
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview

This document is a consolidated reference for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC and on-prem). It covers approved reference architectures, packaging and installation patterns, day-2 operational runbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures. Intended audience: Solutions Engineers, SREs, and Customer Site Reliability teams supporting production private deployments.

Goals
- Provide repeatable, secure deployment patterns for VPC-hosted and on-prem customers.
- Standardize day-2 operations (monitoring, backups, capacity changes, incident triage).
- Define a safe, auditable upgrade and rollback process for releases and model bundles.
- Capture customer requirements and minimum checklist for engagement.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private: VPC-hosted private control plane and on-prem appliance deployments.
- Does not cover Hosted API or Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) specifics.

Owners and Contact
- Deployment lead: Priya Shah (eng-private-deployments)
- SRE lead: Daniel Kim (eng-sre)
- Support escalation: Customer Success oncall (see /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook)

Reference Architectures (high level)

1) VPC-Hosted Private Control Plane (Recommended for cloud-savvy customers)
- Control plane runs in Redwood-managed account or partner-managed control plane inside customer VPC (customer preference).
- Data plane: deployed within customer VPC across 3 AZs for HA (control of egress and KMS).
- Networking: Transit gateway or VPC peering; explicit NAT/egress rules; security groups least privilege.
- Identity: Customer-managed OIDC + SSO for console; KMS/HSM integration for model keys.

Typical components and minimal sizing
| Component | Purpose | Minimum sizing (prod) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Control plane (k8s or managed) | API, auth, orchestration | 3 x t3.medium (non-prod) / 3 x m5.large (prod) | Can be hosted by Redwood for smaller customers |
| Serving cluster (GPUs) | Model inference | Depends on model; 1+ GPU per worker (e.g., p4d/gn5) | Autoscaling recommended |
| Cache/kv (Redis) | Prefix + KV cache for KV-cache acceleration | cluster.t3.medium x3 | Use persistence if using large caches |
| Postgres | Metadata, audit logs | db.m5.large, multi-AZ | Encrypted at rest |

2) On-Prem Appliance Reference (Air-gapped / regulated)
- Delivered as an OVA/container bundle + operator for customer virtualization environments (VMWare, KVM, or bare-metal with container runtime).
- Bundled components: serving runtime, orchestration operator, local artifact store, optional model download service, metrics/alerting stack.
- Hardening: FIPS-compatible crypto where required, offline KMS connector, host-based firewall rules, per-node RBAC.

Packaging and Installation Patterns

- Distribution formats supported:
  - Helm charts (preferred for customers running Kubernetes)
  - Operator + OCI artifact bundle (for air-gapped installs)
  - OVA appliance for legacy virtualization environments

- Install steps (kubernetes, high level):
  1. Preflight checks (networking, DNS, NTP, firewall, required ports).
  2. Provision infra (VMs/instances, disks, GPUs) and attach KMS/HSM if requested.
  3. Install cluster components: ingress, cert-manager, storage class, monitoring stack.
  4. Apply Redwood operator and install control-plane Helm chart with customer values.
  5. Deploy serving clusters and register model artifacts.

- Example helm install command:
  helm repo add redwood https://charts.redwood-inference.internal/charts
  helm upgrade --install redwood-controlplane redwood/controlplane -n redwood --create-namespace -f values.prod.yaml

Preflight checklist (short)
- Network: Customer CNI validated; required ports open (443, 9411, 9090, 9000, GPU drivers e.g., 22 for install).
- Storage: CSI driver, PV capacity >= planned model disk use.
- Time sync: NTP configured across nodes.
- Security: KMS integration or HSM keys provisioned; firewall rules scoped.

Day-2 Operations (Runbooks)

Monitoring and alerting
- Required metrics: per-model p95 latency, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate, Redis latency, error-rate per route.
- SLOs and alert thresholds (suggested):
  - Serving p95 latency: 200ms (alert at > 300ms sustained for 5m)
  - Error rate: >1% requests failed in 5m window (P1)
  - GPU memory pressure: >85% (warn at 75%)
  - KV cache hit-rate below 40% for 15m (investigate caching config)

- Dashboards to include: per-model performance, cost-per-token estimator, node health, network egress breakdown.

Incident triage (high level)
1. Identify scope: single model / single node / cluster-wide.
2. Check control plane health: API server, DB connectivity, queueing backpressure.
3. Check serving cluster: node GPU health, recent scaling events, OOM/killed pods.
4. If customer impact: follow escalation playbook, open SE ticket and attach diagnostics (logs, profiling snapshot, last 100 request traces).

Backups and restore
- Metadata DB: nightly snapshot + binlog replication; store encrypted snapshots to S3-compatible archive.
- Model artifacts: immutable model bundle storage with versioned artifacts; replicate to cold storage per customer RPO.
- Restore procedure (short):
  1. Quiesce writes to metadata DB.
  2. Restore DB snapshot to staging namespace.
  3. Validate metadata integrity and model artifact availability.
  4. Switch traffic after validation.

Capacity management
- Autoscaling policy guidance: use target-based horizontal autoscaler on request queue length + vertical pod autoscaler for worker sizes.
- Capacity runbook: forecast token/sec by traffic profile; reserve burst capacity for model warmup (pre-warming recommended for large models).

Upgrade and Rollback Procedures

Scope of upgrades
- Control plane (API, console), Serving runtime, Model bundle updates, and third-party dependencies (Redis/Postgres).

Pre-upgrade checklist
- Confirm backups exist (DB snapshot and model artifact snapshot).
- Run smoke/e2e tests in staging using the customer config.
- Notify customer of maintenance window and provide rollback plan.
- Ensure node drain window and feature flags set appropriately.

Blue/Green upgrade pattern (recommended)
1. Provision parallel control-plane (green) with new release.
2. Synchronize metadata and model artifacts from blue to green.
3. Run automated regression suite against green using traffic capture.
4. Shift a small percentage of traffic (canary) for 30-60 minutes.
5. If metrics are nominal, ramp to 100% and decommission blue.

Rolling upgrade pattern (for on-prem constrained environments)
1. Upgrade one serving node at a time: cordon -> drain -> apply update -> uncordon.
2. Monitor key metrics for 15m after each node.
3. If any critical alerts (>P1) appear, stop and initiate rollback for that node.

Rollback checklist
- Keep previous release artifacts and operator manifests available.
- Recreate DB schema version if needed using migration rollback script.
- For failed serving runtime upgrade: scale old replica set back up, verify health, then drain/terminate failed nodes.

Example rollback commands (k8s):
- kubectl rollout undo deploy/redwood-serving --namespace redwood
- helm rollback redwood-controlplane 3 --namespace redwood

Customer Requirements Library (minimums before engagement)

Network and Security
- Dedicated VPC or isolated on-prem network segment.
- Customer-managed KMS keys with rotation policy.
- Allowlisting for Redwood maintenance IPs (if customer requests).

Compliance and Data Residency
- Data residency requirement (region) documented and validated.
- Audit log retention and forwarding to customer SIEM configured.

Operational readiness
- Designated customer SRE contact with access to required consoles.
- Maintenance window cadence and SLA expectations agreed.
- Capacity forecast and initial model list + expected QPS.

Minimum checklist (short form)
1. Confirm network reachability and DNS for control plane endpoints.
2. Verify GPU drivers, node-level telemetry, and storage class.
3. KMS/HSM integration validated with key test.
4. Access control (SSO/SCIM) configured for initial admin users.

Change control and compliance
- All upgrades and major config changes require an RFC submitted to eng-private-deployments with owner, risk assessment, and rollback plan.
- For regulated customers, maintain a separate release pipeline that includes signed SBOMs and binary attestations.

Appendices

A. Ports and Firewall Summary
- 443 (HTTPS) - Control plane API and console
- 9411 - Tracing (if enabled)
- 9090 - Prometheus (restricted to monitoring network)
- 9000 - Internal artifact registry (if self-hosted)
- 22 - SSH (install access only; recommend temporary short-lived access)

B. Example values.prod.yaml snippets
redis:
  enabled: true
  persistence: true
  replicaCount: 3
controlPlane:
  replicaCount: 3
  ingressHost: "redwood-cp.customer.example"
  tls: true
serving:
  defaultPoolSize: 4
  gpu: true

C. Troubleshooting quick hits
- High latency, GPU utilization low: check batching config and KV cache hit-rate.
- Serving pods CrashLoopBackOff: review OOMKilled events and increase pod memory limits; check model size vs node GPU memory.
- Slow scale-up: verify autoscaler permissions and cluster quota; consider warm pools.

Summary
This reference is intended to be the single source for engineering and SE teams when scoping, deploying, and operating private Redwood deployments. For new customer engagements, follow the Customer Requirements Library and run preflight checks in the on-boarding checklist.
